requirements.evidence: CreateQueue (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:16-38) authorizes, trims and validates the name to 1-255 chars, slugifies the slug (or the name when no slug is given), checks per-entity uniqueness and converts a unique-index QueryException into a ValidationException. UpdateQueue (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:20-66) takes nullable named arguments, keeps the queue's own slug through `whereKeyNot`, and adds no delete action. SetQueueAccess upserts for a non-empty list, deletes for an empty one, rejects cross-entity pairs and unknown or non-string entries (`Rule::enum`, 'string'), and only logs a revoke when a row was deleted (`->delete() > 0`). QueuePolicy::call lets managers through without a grant and denies a non-array value (`is_array($access->permissions)`). CallNextTicket authorizes after the lock and the active check (CallNextTicket.php:32). Ticket::call runs lock, inactive check, authorize, then the LogicException (Ticket.php:88-109). Migration, enum, model, factory and docs all match the contract. One note: the policy relies on `User::membershipFor`, which is not in the diff and is assumed to exist already.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes live in app/Actions and authorize inside through `Gate::forUser(...)->authorize` against an auto-discovered policy. QueueAccess sets `#[Fillable([...])]`. The migration has a reversible `down()`. business-rules.md, database-schema.md and the CHANGELOG 'Added' section are updated. Two small deviations: the migration's round timestamp `2026_10_29_120000` suggests it was hand-named rather than made with `make:migration`, and a new `Actions/Concerns` trait adds a small helper layer, although it is justified by the shared create/update rules.

security.evidence: Every new action authorizes before any validation or write (CreateQueue.php:18, UpdateQueue.php:28, SetQueueAccess.php:29). Both call paths now enforce `call` instead of plain membership (Ticket.php:106, CallNextTicket.php:32). The policy requires role Employee plus a grant for that exact queue. Corrupted JSON denies access. Permissions are checked against the enum. Mass assignment is restricted with Fillable. No weakness found.

tests.evidence: The tests are thorough: CreateQueueTest, UpdateQueueTest, SetQueueAccessTest, QueuePolicyTest, CallAuthorizationTest and QueueAccessModelTest. They cover the 255/256 name boundary, simulated unique-index races, every call mode, inactive-before-authorize ordering, authorize-before-LogicException, corrupted permission data, audit events and no-op revokes. Existing CallNextTicket tests were updated to use a manager rather than weakened. Gap: the 'non-member' case in CreateQueueTest (and 'stranger' in UpdateQueueTest) is actually an owner of another entity, so a user with no membership at all is not tested for create/update.

simplicity.evidence: The code is lean overall and the trait avoids duplicating name/slug logic between Create and Update. Some extras go beyond what the task needs: SetQueueAccess::lockQueue adds a queue-row lock around a single upsert/delete that the unique index already protects, and the factory has two helper states (`forMembership`, `forQueue`). `isSlugConflict` matches driver-specific message strings (NormalizesQueueAttributes.php:62-68) where checking the SQLSTATE code would be simpler.

readability.evidence: Methods are small and well named (normalizeName, assertSlugAvailable, revoke, validatedPermissions). PHPDoc explains intent, for example the lock-order comments in Ticket::call and the corrupted-JSON comment in QueuePolicy::call. Style matches sibling files, and there is no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the task: actions, policy, model, factory, migration, enum, call-path enforcement, docs, CHANGELOG, tests and shared Pest helpers (`managerOf`, `memberWithRole`). The CallNextTicket comment edit reflects the new shared queue lock. There is no UI and no delete action.

issues.explanation: The 'non-member' case is `memberWithRole(Entity::factory()->create(), UserRole::Owner)`, so it repeats the other-entity-manager case and never tests a user with no membership at all (the same applies to 'stranger' in UpdateQueueTest).
The policy depends on `User::membershipFor()`, which this diff does not add, so correctness depends on an existing helper that cannot be seen here.

Slug conflicts are detected by matching driver-specific substrings of the exception message. This is brittle across databases and index names; checking the SQLSTATE integrity-violation code plus the index would be more robust.
The round timestamp suggests the migration file was hand-named rather than created with `php artisan make:migration` as the conventions require.
The extra queue-row `lockForUpdate` around a single upsert/delete adds complexity that the unique index and updateOrCreate mostly cover already.

review.summary: The change adds CreateQueue, UpdateQueue and SetQueueAccess actions, a QueuePolicy, the queue_access table with its model, factory and enum, and `call` authorization on both CallNextTicket and Ticket::call in the required order, with docs and CHANGELOG updated. It meets the contract and edge cases with strong tests (races, every call mode, corrupted data, audit logging). The only gaps are minor: a mislabeled non-member test case, brittle detection of slug conflicts from the exception message, and a migration that looks hand-named, so I would approve with nits.
